name: Millpond Gnawer
lore: It lives under the mill wheel and comes out when the wheel stops. Millers used to drown them by the sack. Nobody has the time now, so the gnawers have the pond, and the miller works the day shift only.
visualBrief: Otter-shaped, low and long, with a flat paddle tail and teeth too big for the jaw. Wet fur clumps into spines along the back; one ear is always chewed short.

name: Tallgrass Tick
lore: Waist-high grass on the road out of Millcross, and a hand-sized tick on every third stalk. They drop when a shadow passes and hold on hard. New expedition hands learn to walk the ruts and not the verge, usually once.
visualBrief: A flat grey disc the size of a spread hand, eight barbed legs folded under, swelling dark red when it feeds. Reads as a stone until it moves.

name: Chaff Crawler
lore: Grain dust settles in the yard behind the mill and something under it grows fat. The crawler pushes up through the chaff pile, walks a straight line at whatever it hears, and goes back under when it stops hearing. It is slow enough to walk away from and stubborn enough that nobody bothers.
visualBrief: A hunched armored grub, chest-high, plated in overlapping dust-caked shell. Mandibles hang low and wide; a pale grain crust coats every seam.

name: Hedgerow Thorn
lore: A field hedge that stopped being a hedge. It holds its patch of road and lashes anything that steps into reach. Farmers cut it back every spring and it is always back by harvest, a little further into the lane.
visualBrief: A squat wall of woven bramble with a knot at the center that opens like a mouth. Long whip-canes trail from the top edge, tipped with black thorns.

name: Strayling Pup
lore: Ashfang packs leave their young at the edge of the meadow while the grown ones hunt. A pup will not face a standing person. It circles, bites the back of the leg, and runs for the treeline to see if you follow.
visualBrief: Knee-high, all shoulder and no weight, rust-orange fur with faint ember markings not yet joined into a pattern. Ears too large; ribs showing.

name: Roadcrow Flock
lore: They follow the road because the road feeds them. Since the war they follow travelers instead of carts, and they no longer wait for a body to stop moving. A flock will strip a pack open in the time it takes to cut one down.
visualBrief: Six to ten ragged black birds moving as one shape, wings frayed at the tips. Beaks are hooked and blunt from bone, and each carries a scrap of cloth in its claws.

name: Lampwing Moth
lore: They gather at the tallow lamps along the Millcross road and burn without dying. A lampwing throws its heat outward when it is startled, which is often. Carters cover their lamps now and take the road by feel.
visualBrief: Wingspan the width of a shoulder, wings lit from inside like paper over a candle. Body is a soot-black cinder; the eyes glow the same orange as the wings.

name: Sackrat Swarm
lore: The refugee stores brought rats and the rats brought more rats. They swarm a standing sack, and lately they swarm a standing person. The Quartermaster counts losses in meals, and the sackrats cost her more meals last season than the raiders did.
visualBrief: A moving carpet of grey bodies, twenty or more, with grain husks stuck in the fur. No leader shape; the swarm bulges toward whatever it wants.

name: Ditchlight Wisp
lore: A cold light over the flooded ditches south of the mill. It drifts toward anyone carrying a lamp, as if it wants a closer look, and the water it leaves on a person does not dry. Old carters say it is only marsh gas. Old carters also walk the far verge.
visualBrief: A hand-sized pale blue light with no lamp around it, trailing a thin ribbon of mist. Water beads in the air where it has been.

name: Cinderhen
lore: Embervale keeps its birds near the forge heat and the birds have grown to like it too well. A cinderhen nests in warm slag and defends the nest against anything that walks past. Children are told to throw a coat over one and carry it out. Most of them only try it once.
visualBrief: A heavy ground bird the size of a dog, feathers banded black and ember-orange, with bare grey legs and spurs. Ash puffs from the plumage when it flaps.

name: Slagheap Grub
lore: They eat the poured-off waste from Embervale's forges and hold the heat in their bodies for days. A grub will not chase, but it will roll over whatever is in front of it. The smiths turn the heaps twice a week to break them up.
visualBrief: A pale segmented grub as long as an arm, skin translucent over a dull red glow. Slag crust flakes off the back where it has cooled.

name: Graveturf Creeper
lore: Norhollow buries its dead behind the palisade, and it buries them properly. What crawls out of the outer fields is from the ones it could not reach in time. A creeper is small, cold, and wrong to touch. The bell-wardens come out and burn the turf, and for a season the field is quiet.
visualBrief: A low four-limbed thing of matted sod and root, no face, with a hollow where a face should sit. Black dust falls from it and does not blow away.

name: Palisade Borer
lore: It eats standing timber and Norhollow is a town made of standing timber. The palisade guard walks the line twice a day tapping stakes and listening for the hollow ones. A stake that answers hollow gets pulled and replaced before dark, every time, no argument.
visualBrief: A thick beetle the length of a forearm, shell the grey-brown of weathered oak, with rasping jaws set forward like a chisel. Sawdust packs the leg joints.

name: Tideflat Nipper
lore: The flats south of Rooktide empty twice a day and fill again, and the nippers come in with the water. They take toes off waders who stand still. Rooktide children learn to keep moving on the flats before they learn to read a tide mark.
visualBrief: A flat grey fish the length of a hand with a jaw hinged too wide, moving in threes and fours. Silver belly, gill slits ringed dark.

name: Thatch Mite
lore: Rooktide rebuilt its roofs with new reed and the mites came with the reed. They drop from the eaves onto whatever passes under. It is a small nuisance in a town that has survived a large one, and the elder says so often.
visualBrief: A pale straw-colored mite the size of a thumb, moving in loose clusters. Legs are hair-fine; the body reads as a seed head until it turns.

name: Rookshade
lore: The shape of a rook, cast on a wall with no rook and no sun to cast it. It follows people who are alone and calls the flats birds down on them. It has never touched anyone. Nobody in Rooktide has worked out what it wants, and the town has decided it can wait.
visualBrief: A flat bird-shaped shadow that moves across surfaces rather than through air. Edges fray into grey smoke; no depth, no eyes.

name: Bramble Shoot
lore: The Thornveil skirmishers plant them along their approach lanes and let them grow. A shoot cannot follow anyone, so it does the next best thing and takes the ground. Walking the bramble without a bramble-kin guide costs blood and time, and the skirmishers count on both.
visualBrief: A waist-high tangle of green cane with a woody core, bristling outward. New growth is bright and soft; the old wood is black and hooked.

name: Thicket Hopper
lore: It clears a bramble wall in one jump and lands on whatever is behind it. Hoppers do not hunt so much as arrive. The bramble-kin say you never see the one that gets you, and they say it as a rule of the forest, not a joke.
visualBrief: A leaf-green cricket the size of a cat, with thick spring legs and a wedge head. Wing cases rattle dry when it takes off.

name: Veil Cub
lore: Something in the Thornveil raises litters and does not stay with them. The cubs hunt in pairs, badly, and learn on whoever is walking the lanes that season. Nobody has seen the grown animal. Everyone has an opinion about it.
visualBrief: Low-slung, cat-shaped, bark-brown with a broken pale stripe down the spine. The paws are oversized and the eyes sit forward, wide and flat.

name: Wharf Scuttler
lore: They live under the Gildmark piers and come up through the boards at night. Dock hands lose fingers to them and lose the day's pay for reporting it late. The harbor keeps a scuttler bounty on the board, unpaid for two seasons.
visualBrief: A crab the width of a dinner plate, shell tarnished gold-brown with barnacle scarring. One claw is twice the size of the other and always raised.

name: Tally-Walker
lore: The Builder School made them to count crates along the wharf, and a few were left counting after their stone ran low. A tally-walker will not let a load past it that it has not marked. It has no way to mark anything anymore, so nothing gets past.
visualBrief: A knee-high brass frame on four stiff legs, a slate board bolted to its back, chalk stub still clamped in one arm. Movement is jerky and evenly timed.

name: Ashfield Crawler
lore: The smallest thing the Ashvale ground makes. It comes up wherever a body went under without a burial and drags itself toward warmth. One is easy. The trouble is that one means the field under your boots is full of them.
visualBrief: An armless torso-sized shape of packed ash and cloth scraps, pulling itself on two thin fore-limbs. A cold black seam runs where the mouth would be.

name: Millrace Lurker
lore: Grown from the same water as the gnawers, and grown too big for the pond. It waits in the millrace where the current hides its shape and takes what comes to drink. Millcross lost two dogs and a cart horse to one before anyone believed the boy who saw it.
visualBrief: A thick-bodied river beast the length of a man, hide slick and grey-green, with a broad flat head and small eyes set high. Webbed forelimbs end in blunt claws.

name: Strayling Yearling
lore: A pup that lived through its first winter and its first fight. The ember markings have joined into a line down the flank, which is how the pack reads its rank. A yearling still circles, but it circles closer, and it comes back.
visualBrief: Waist-high and lean, rust-orange with a continuous ember-red stripe along each side. Old bite scars mark the shoulders; the tail is half gone.

name: Cordknot Effigy
lore: Millcross families tie a knot in a cord for every member the road took. Somewhere in the refugee camps a cord got long enough to stand up on its own. It stays near the tents and makes the things around it harder to put down.
visualBrief: A person-shaped bundle of knotted rope and patched wool, no head, cords trailing to the ground. Each knot is a different cord and a different color.

name: Tollroad Wrecker
lore: Men who set a rope across the trade road and call it a toll. They started the season taking coin and ended it taking carts. None of them are from anywhere near Millcross, and all of them came through it.
visualBrief: A heavy man in mismatched salvage plate over travel wool, a cart axle carried as a club. A stolen wax-seal ring hangs on a cord at the neck.

name: Bramble Stalker
lore: A shoot that pulled its own roots up and learned to walk on them. The skirmishers do not plant these; they only stopped cutting them down. A stalker moves at the pace of the wind through the canes, which is exactly why nobody hears it coming.
visualBrief: A man-height bundle of green cane walking on a knot of trailing roots. Two whip-arms of hooked thorn; no head, only a dark hollow at chest height.

name: Veil Spearling
lore: The youngest of the bramble-kin, given a harness of three spears and one rule: never be where you were seen. A spearling throws, moves, and throws again from somewhere else. They are not good at it yet. There are a great many of them.
visualBrief: A slight figure in bramble-woven leathers, face wrapped, a three-spear harness across the back. Bare arms scratched from shoulder to wrist.

name: Thornhusk Weaver
lore: It strings its web between the canes at head height and dresses it in bramble husks so the line reads as more bramble. Whatever walks into it stops walking. The weaver takes its time after that, and it is never far away.
visualBrief: A long-legged spider the size of a helmet, body dressed in glued-on thorn husks. It sits still enough to pass for a dead bramble knot.

name: Stakeline Hound
lore: Norhollow ran war dogs along the palisade line and the war outlasted the handlers. The hounds still walk the stakeline, still bark at the same hour, and no longer know whose side anyone is on. The guard feeds them anyway. Nobody has ordered otherwise.
visualBrief: A rangy grey-coated hound with a cut ear and a rotted leather collar bearing a tally of notches. The ribs show; the gait does not.

name: Tallyknot Wight
lore: A palisade guard counts the dead on a knotted belt cord and adds a knot every evening. One of them kept counting after his own name should have gone on it. He walks the outer fields now, still adding, and the cord has grown longer than he is tall.
visualBrief: A gaunt figure in palisade-guard leathers, a knotted belt cord dragging behind for several paces. The face is unmarked and the eyes are dark all the way through.

name: Forge-Ash Hound
lore: Embervale slept its hounds by the forge floor for warmth and bred them for it for four generations. They run hot to the touch and they run all night. When the banner marched, the kennels emptied themselves and followed as far as the plain.
visualBrief: A deep-chested hound with a coat the color of banked coals and ash caked into the shoulder fur. Breath steams even in summer.

name: Emberpit Digger
lore: A slagheap grub that lived long enough to grow legs and a temper. It digs under the ember pits and comes up wherever the ground is warmest, which is usually under a working smith. Embervale lost a forge house to one and rebuilt it on stone.
visualBrief: A hunched digging insect the size of a hog, front limbs flattened into spades, plates glowing dull red at the joints. Ash drifts from it constantly.

name: Tideline Drowner
lore: Rooktide nearly emptied out once, and not everyone who left made it to a road. What the tide brings back walks the flats at low water and goes under again when it fills. The elder has them carried up and buried properly. He does it himself, each time, and does not talk about it.
visualBrief: A waterlogged body in ruined tide-grey clothes, skin bleached pale, weed and old rope caught at the ankles. It drips constantly and leaves wet prints on dry stone.

name: Saltmarsh Wisp
lore: It sits over the salt marsh where the old town road went under. Fishermen use it to find the channel and never say so out loud. It lets them, most nights. On the nights it does not, the boat comes back empty.
visualBrief: A drifting sheet of pale green light about the size of a sail, thin enough to see the marsh through. Salt crusts on anything it passes over.

name: Frostbitten Ox
lore: Expedition draft oxen that walked off the ice road and did not die of it. They graze on nothing anyone can see and charge anything that crosses their line. The camp still keeps their names on the tally board, unstruck, because nobody wants to be the one to strike them.
visualBrief: A heavy shaggy ox with rime frozen into the coat in plates and one horn snapped short. A rotted harness strap still hangs from the neck.

name: Rime Shrike
lore: It hunts the open shelf where there is nothing to hide behind, and it does not need to hide. A shrike dives, cuts, and climbs before the cold lets a man raise a shield. It keeps what it takes on an ice spur, hung in a row.
visualBrief: A frost-white raptor with a long hooked beak and black wingtips. Talons carry a thin permanent glaze of ice.

name: Cranehook Automaton
lore: Built to swing cargo off a hull and set it down gently. The Builder School sold a batch to the harbor before the wards on them were finished. Now one works the empty quay at night, lifting nothing, setting it down gently, and taking the arm off anyone who steps into the arc.
visualBrief: A chest-high brass and iron frame on a swiveling base, one long hook arm counterweighted at the back. Magic-stone housing glows faint amber through a grille.

name: Bilge Crawler
lore: It comes off the ships and it never comes off alone. Gildmark's harbor masters know which hulls carry them and charge the berth accordingly. The ledger has a line for it. That is as close as the port gets to admitting the problem.
visualBrief: An eel-bodied thing with six crab legs, arm-length, slick black and glistening. It moves fast across dry boards and faster in water.

name: Shovel Wight
lore: Burial parties go out to the Ashvale Front between the fighting and they do not always all come back. A shovel wight still has the tool and still has the ground it was working. It swings on anything that comes near the row it was digging.
visualBrief: A slouched figure in banded mourning cloth gone grey, a long-handled shovel held two-handed and low. Where the face was there is packed grave dirt.

name: Ashvale Carrion Hound
lore: Not a dog that ate the dead. A dog that the dead ground made, out of what was lying there. It runs the burial rows in packs of four and it does not eat what it kills. The bell-wardens go out after them with holy work, and it is work, not mercy.
visualBrief: A hound-shaped thing of grey sinew and grave cloth, ribs open to the air with nothing behind them. The eyes are two cold voids; it leaves no prints.

name: Toll-Struck Warden
lore: A bell-warden went out to the front to ring the field clean and rang until his heart stopped. The holy work did not stop with him. He still walks the rows, still tolling, and the void things will not come within thirty paces of him. Neither will anyone else.
visualBrief: A bell-warden in bronze-trimmed robes, a hand bell fused into the right palm, standing too straight. A steady pale light shows through the seams of the robe.

name: Millroad Brigand
lore: Wreckers who learned the road and stopped needing a rope across it. They take the cart, the horse, and the seal off the letters, and they leave the letters. That last part is deliberate. Somebody pays them for what the letters said.
visualBrief: A wiry figure in road-worn leathers with a scarf pulled to the eyes, short blade in one hand and a stolen tally-cord at the belt. Boots better than the rest of the kit.

name: Quarrystone Beetle
lore: It grows its shell out of whatever it eats, and it eats the quarry face west of Millcross. A full-grown one turns a hammer. The quarry crews work around them and have stopped calling that a delay.
visualBrief: A boulder-backed beetle as wide as a cart, shell grown through with grey stone and quartz veining. Six thick legs; the head barely clears the ground.

name: Gallows-Meadow Shade
lore: Millcross hanged three wreckers in the meadow the first winter of the war and left the frame standing as a warning. The frame came down in a storm. What stood under it did not. It keeps to the flattened grass and it will not let a lamp near it.
visualBrief: A tall thin figure of grey mist with rope-marks where the neck would be, feet a hand's width off the ground. Grass under it lies flat and stays flat.

name: Bramble Warden
lore: The skirmishers grow one at each of the four ways into the deep veil and feed it the bodies of whoever tried the fifth. A warden holds a lane by itself. It is the only sentry the bramble-kin trust to never fall asleep.
visualBrief: A hunched mass of black woody cane two men wide, standing on braided root legs. Four whip-arms; a crown of upward thorns where a head should be.

name: Thornveil Spearhand
lore: A spearling who lived long enough to get good. A spearhand throws once, from cover, and is two lanes away before the shaft lands. They take no prisoners and leave no wounded, and they will tell you plainly that carrying either through the bramble is not possible.
visualBrief: Lean, bramble-woven leathers stained green-black, face wrapped, six spears in a back harness. Old thorn scars mark both forearms in even rows.

name: Sapdrinker Swarm
lore: They drink the bramble dry and move on together when a stand of cane dies. A swarm crossing a lane sounds like rain on a roof and takes about as long to pass. Anything caught in the middle of that comes out lighter.
visualBrief: A dense cloud of finger-long green flies moving as one column. Where the swarm has fed, the cane behind it is pale and hollow.

name: Frostfell Stalker
lore: White on white, and it knows it. The stalker walks the expedition's ice road at a distance for a full day before it closes. The camp keeps a fire burning at both ends of the road for exactly that reason, and it works about half the time.
visualBrief: A long-bodied white cat, shoulder-high, with a flat broad face and no visible ears. Pads leave shallow prints that fill in behind it.

name: Oathtablet Sentry
lore: Cindervast built them to stand at gates and the Stoneguard carried the last of them north. A sentry checks whoever passes against an oath cut into the tablet on its chest, and the tablet names a city that is not there. Nobody passes. That is not a failure of the sentry.
visualBrief: A squat iron figure the height of a man, cracked ceremonial plating, a stone oath-tablet bolted across the chest. Frost fills the letters cut into the tablet.

name: Hoarfrost Wisp
lore: It forms where a person sat down on the ice and did not get up. There are a great many of them along the old survey line. They drift toward warmth and take it, and the warmth is all they take.
visualBrief: A pale white light the size of a head, wrapped in a slow spiral of ice crystals. The ground beneath it turns milky and hard.

name: Trench Gnawer
lore: It works the cut lines both towns dug and then abandoned. A gnawer widens a trench as it feeds, so the diggings are longer now than either army ever made them. Walk a trench on the Ashvale Front and you are walking through something's throat.
visualBrief: A broad low quadruped of grave earth and splintered timber, jaw wider than the skull. Cold black dust pours from the joints as it moves.

name: Standard-Bearer Husk
lore: It carries a banner with the colors worn off, so neither town claims it and both shoot at it. Where it plants the pole, the other dead stand faster and stay standing longer. It has planted the pole in the same spot forty times. The ground there will not hold grass.
visualBrief: An upright corpse in mixed iron-red and hollow-green scraps, both hands locked on a bare banner pole. The cloth at the top is grey rag with no device left.

name: Ashen Torchbearer
lore: The Ash Prophet sends them ahead of a raid to light what the raid will take. A torchbearer does not fight for ground and does not hold any. It burns a farm, a fence, a bridge, and walks on to the next one, and it does not look back at the work.
visualBrief: A soot-wrapped figure carrying a long pitch torch in both hands, face bare and unburned. Cinder-black cloth, relic-violet thread stitched at the cuffs.

name: Cratershell Crawler
lore: It wears the ground it grew in, which on the Ashvale Front means broken shields and burial stones. The shell is cold enough to sting a bare hand. Cut through it and there is nothing warm underneath either.
visualBrief: A cart-sized crawler under a dome of fused shield fragments and grave slate. Six pale legs; the shell edge scrapes furrows in the dirt.

name: Relicglow Moth
lore: They breed in the violet afterglow that never left the fallen city and they carry a little of it out with them on their wings. Scavengers follow the moths inward because the moths know where the glow is thickest. Scavengers who follow them all the way in do not come out.
visualBrief: A pale moth the width of two hands, wings washed with a faint violet light that pulses when it beats. The body is chalk-white and furred.

name: Soot-Wrapped Scavenger
lore: The Column digs the ruin districts for relic scrap and posts scavengers to keep other diggers off. They fight over ground that killed a city and they consider that the point. Ask one what he is looking for and he will tell you honestly. It never sounds better for the honesty.
visualBrief: A figure in layered soot-marked wraps and a scavenged half-helm, a pry bar in one hand and a short blade in the other. A relic token hangs open at the throat, not hidden.

name: Slagpit Hulk
lore: Embervale poured its forge waste into the same pit for forty years, and one winter the pit stood up. It walks a slow circuit of the works and knocks down anything built across its path. The smiths moved the road instead of fighting it, twice.
visualBrief: A lumbering shape of cooled slag and clinker, two heads taller than a man, seams glowing dull orange. No face; the head is a fused lump.

name: Palisade Breaker
lore: It came down out of the moor the second winter and took out eleven stakes in one night. Norhollow rebuilt the line and set a watch on that quarter. The tally at the guard house counts the stakes it has taken since, not the men, because the men are counted elsewhere.
visualBrief: A stooped grey-skinned giant, one and a half times a man's height, with a barked hide and hands like mallets. Broken stake-timber is caught in the knuckles.

name: Ledger Hound
lore: Gildmark sells bound war-beasts by the crate and keeps a few for the warehouse floor. A ledger hound is warded, harnessed, and set on anyone whose paperwork does not clear. The harbor does not call this a guard animal. The harbor calls it an audit.
visualBrief: A tall short-haired hound in a brass-studded harness, ward runes cut into the plates. A wax-seal tag hangs from the collar, cracked and unreadable.

name: Ashfang Pack-Leader
lore: The one the brutes walk behind. A pack-leader does not lead from the front and does not need to; it picks the target and the pack reads the choice off its shoulders. Kill the leader and the pack does not scatter. It picks another one before the body cools.
visualBrief: A heavy-shouldered beast the size of a plough horse, rust-orange coat over ember-red markings that spread across the whole back. Both ears are gone; the teeth are worn flat.

name: Millstone Warden
lore: A Builder School piece sold to the mill to turn the stone when the water ran low. When the mill burned, the warden kept turning, and it has been walking the ruin in a circle ever since. It will not step outside the ring it has worn into the floor. It will kill anything that steps inside it.
visualBrief: A broad brass-and-timber frame carrying a cracked millstone as a shield across the chest. It walks a fixed circle; the stone grinds when it turns.

name: Bramble Drake
lore: It does not fly. It pushes through the deep veil at chest height and takes the canes down with it, which is how you know where it has been. The bramble-kin do not hunt it. They have a word for the sound it makes and they use the word as an order to leave.
visualBrief: A low four-legged drake the length of a cart, scaled bark-brown with green moss in the plate seams. The skull is broad and blunt, built for pushing.

name: Briar-Caller
lore: Bramble-kin who studied at an Elements School and came home to use it on the canes. A caller can close a lane behind a raiding party in the time it takes to walk through it. Warded steel shrugs the work off. Warded steel does not clear a path.
visualBrief: A wiry figure in bramble-woven wraps with a magic-stone pouch at the hip and both palms scarred green. Cane growth follows the hands when they move.

name: Rime Drake
lore: It nests in the pressure ridges where the ice buckles and it does not leave the shelf. The expedition marked three nests on the survey map and then stopped marking them. Knowing where they are has not once helped anybody.
visualBrief: A serpentine drake the length of a boat, scales frost-white over pale blue, with a narrow head and a fin crest along the spine. Breath fogs heavily even on cold air.

name: Icelocked Oathkeeper
lore: The Stoneguard who walked north with the last sentries and stopped where the sentries stopped. The ice took them standing, in order, still in their ranks. They came out of it a generation later and formed up again, and the order they formed in was the right one.
visualBrief: A frozen figure in cracked ceremonial plate, ice grown through the joints and holding a bent shield to the body. An oath-tablet pendant hangs frozen against the breastplate.

name: Gravetide Wight
lore: It rises with the ground when the rain lifts the shallow rows, which is why the towns call it a tide. A wight is one burial that came up carrying pieces of four others. The bell-wardens say the cure is a proper grave, and they are right, and there is no time.
visualBrief: A tall shambling figure assembled from more than one body, mismatched iron-red and hollow-green cloth fused together. Cold black seams glow where the pieces join.

name: Flagrot Swarm
lore: They breed in fallen banners and eat the cloth first and the pole second. A swarm rolling across the front reads as a low grey wind. Both armies have lost their colors to it in the same week and neither will admit which week.
visualBrief: A rolling cloud of small black flies shot through with grey banner threads. It leaves the ground behind it bare and faintly cold.

name: Bell-Scoured Penitent
lore: The Bell School's holy work burns the void out of a war-scar body. Sometimes the body keeps walking after it is clean. A penitent follows the bell-wardens at a distance, helps them where it can, and will not be sent away. The wardens have stopped trying.
visualBrief: A thin figure in scorched bell-warden robes, skin bleached bone-white, a brass key still on the collar. A faint steady light shows at the mouth and eyes.

name: Ashen Drum-Caller
lore: The Column has no bells and wants none, so it keeps time on a drum instead. The drum-caller sets the pace of a raid and the raiders match it without looking. Kill the caller and the raid does not stop; it only stops being a raid and starts being a mob.
visualBrief: A soot-wrapped figure with a wide hide drum slung at the hip, both sticks bone. Relic-violet thread is worked through the drum head in a broken crown pattern.

name: Relicslag Crawler
lore: The relic did not only kill the city; it changed what the city was made of. A crawler is a street's worth of that stone, walking. It carries the cold of the fall in it, and things that have been near it for long enough stop wanting to eat.
visualBrief: A wide low mass of fused masonry moving on stubby stone limbs, violet light bleeding from the cracks. Melted door hinges and window bars stick out of the back.

name: Broken-Crown Sentinel
lore: It guarded the ruler's hall and it is still guarding the ruler's hall, though the hall is four walls and no roof. The Stoneguard leave it alone out of respect for the office it was built to serve. The Cindered leave it alone for the opposite reason.
visualBrief: A tall iron automaton in ceremonial plating, a broken-crown device raised on the shield. Soot has blacked it entirely except where the shield device has been kept polished.

name: Cindered Revenant
lore: The rebellion the relic answered had thousands in the streets. Some of them are still in the streets. A revenant runs the same route it ran on the last day and strikes at anything wearing a crest. It cannot read a crest anymore, so a buckle will do.
visualBrief: A charred running figure, clothing burned into the skin, one arm ending at the elbow. Heat shimmers off it and its footprints scorch.

name: Harbor Assessor
lore: The Builder School's proof that automata can do more than lift. It was set to weigh cargo and stop what did not match the manifest, and its manifest is four seasons out of date. Nothing on the quay matches it now. The harbor works the other quay and files the loss under upkeep.
visualBrief: A man-high brass figure with a scale arm on one side and a heavy weighted fist on the other. A wax-seal plate is set into the chest, the seal long since melted flat.

name: Slag Drake
lore: It came for the heat of Embervale's forges and stayed for the food. The banner tried to drive it off twice and lost eight men doing it. Now the town leaves a hog out at the pit twice a month and calls that a solved problem.
visualBrief: A squat four-legged drake with iron-red scales and a hide crusted in cooled slag. Short wings it does not use; the jaw glows between the teeth.

name: Hollowmoor Giant
lore: It comes down off the open moor when the wind turns, and the wind turning is the only warning anyone gets. Norhollow rings the danger code and everybody outside the palisade runs for a gate. Twice it has reached a gate first.
visualBrief: A gaunt grey giant two men high, hollow-cheeked, with long thin arms and a chest that sounds hollow when struck. Furs and stolen palisade rope are wound around the waist.

name: Warscar Maw
lore: Where the fighting was worst and the burying was worst, the ground makes something with a mouth in it. A maw does not hunt outward. It waits in the low ground and takes what the ground funnels to it, and after four seasons of war the ground funnels a great deal.
visualBrief: A hunched slab of grave earth and rusted mail, four times a man's bulk, split across the front by a long vertical mouth. Cold black light shows between the teeth.

name: Shroudweaver
lore: It pulls the burial cloth off the shallow rows and works it into a grey fog that hangs at knee height. Inside the fog a person's own hands go cold and slow. The bell-wardens ring the fog apart when they can spare the wardens, and lately they cannot.
visualBrief: A stooped many-armed shape made of layered grave shrouds, no body under the cloth. Trailing threads reach out along the ground for several paces.

name: Siege-Rot Hulk
lore: Both towns dragged siege engines onto the plain and neither dragged them off. The timber rotted where it stood, over ground full of the unburied, and the ground took it. It still moves toward a palisade line when it can find one.
visualBrief: A walking wreck of siege timber and iron banding held together by grey sinew, twice a man's height. Antimagic runes are still cut into the plates and mean nothing now.

name: Bellwarden Revenant
lore: A whole warden company went out to clear the burial rows and rang until the last of them fell. What stands there now still does the work and cannot be called off. It will strike a war-scar and it will strike a living soldier, and it does not tell them apart anymore.
visualBrief: A robed figure whose bell-warden vestments have gone stiff and pale, a hand bell held out at arm's length. A hard white light burns behind the eyes and inside the bell.

name: Violet-Ash Drake
lore: It nests in the ruin districts where the afterglow is thickest and it has fed on nothing else for a generation. What it breathes out is not fire and does not burn. The Cindered call it the second fall, and they mean the phrase plainly.
visualBrief: A slender winged drake with cinder-black scales and a violet glow along every seam. The wing membranes are thin enough to show the light through.

name: Rebellion Echo
lore: Not a ghost of one person. The noise a crowd makes, left standing in a square after the crowd is gone. It moves through the ruin districts as a sound first, and what is already in the ruin districts wakes up and follows it.
visualBrief: A shifting crowd-shaped blur of grey figures with no faces, never fully solid, spread across half a street. The sound of many voices arrives before the shape does.

name: Relic Hulk
lore: Cindervast was full of workshops when it fell and the relic did not spare them. This is a forge house and everything that was inside it, fused and standing. It burns hot enough that the Column will not dig within two streets of one.
visualBrief: A hulking mass of melted iron tools, anvil stubs, and brick, taller than a cart. The core glows white; the outer crust is cinder-black and flaking.

name: Hoarfell Giant
lore: It walks the deep shelf where the expedition's maps stop. Nobody has driven one off and nobody has needed to; they do not come south. The survey teams that meet one simply do not send back the sheet for that quarter.
visualBrief: A pale blue-grey giant three men high, ice grown over the shoulders like a mantle. It carries a shaft of glacier ice as a club and drags one leg.

name: Snowblind Shade
lore: It comes with the white weather and it is the white weather, as far as anyone standing in it can tell. A shade takes a person's sense of direction first and their warmth second. The expedition ropes its crews together and does not explain why anymore.
visualBrief: A tall streak of driving snow that holds a person's outline for a moment at a time. Nothing solid at the center; the wind bends around a shape that is not there.

name: Bramble Mother
lore: Every bramble wall in the eastern veil runs back to her, root under root. The skirmishers feed her and do not pretend it is anything else. She has held the deep veil against three armies, and none of the three wrote down what stopped them.
visualBrief: A vast rooted mass of black cane the size of a cottage, the front opened into a hollow like a doorway. Green new growth crowns the top; older wood beneath is bone-dry and hooked.

name: Bound War-Beast
lore: Gildmark sells these by the crate to both towns and ships them out of the only deepwater port on this coast. A crate that goes over the side in a storm opens on the beach a week later. The harbor has a word for the ones that get loose, and the word is shrinkage.
visualBrief: A heavy horned quadruped in a riveted war harness, ward runes stamped along the barding. The harness has been chewed through at the shoulder and hangs open.

name: Crateyard Colossus
lore: The largest thing the Builder School has ever sold, and it was sold to move stacks, not people. It clears the crate yard on a fixed round and stacks whatever is loose. Two dock hands went into a stack last winter and the round did not change.
visualBrief: A four-armed brass giant three men high on a wide tracked base, magic-stone housings glowing amber at the hips. Every surface is dented and stamped with harbor marks.

name: Crossroads Reaver
lore: The wreckers who worked the Millcross roads long enough to buy proper plate with what they took. A reaver does not stop a cart to rob it. He stops it because the road behind him needs to stay closed for an hour, and somebody is paying for the hour.
visualBrief: A broad man in good salvaged plate over patched wool, a long-hafted axe carried across the shoulders. Three wax-seal rings on a cord, none of them his.

name: Mourning-Cloth Wight
lore: Embervale bands its dead in mourning cloth and burns them properly, and the town has been proud of that for four generations. The season the caravans burned, there was not time to do it properly. These are the ones from that season, and the town knows exactly which ones they are.
visualBrief: A half-burned figure in banded mourning cloth, the cloth still smoldering at the edges. It moves fast and low; embers fall from it and go out behind it.

name: Frontline Devourer
lore: A maw that grew legs and stopped waiting. It walks the line between the two towns and takes from whichever side is closer that day, which has made it the one thing both banners agree on. They have never once agreed enough to hunt it together.
visualBrief: A long-limbed thing of grave earth and broken mail, hunched to a man's height but wider than a cart, mouths opening along the ribs. Cold black dust hangs where it has passed.

name: Unburied Host
lore: Not one body. A season's worth of them, moving in the shape a company moves in, because that is the last shape they were taught. The host does not charge. It arrives, and what is already on the field stands up and falls in behind it.
visualBrief: A loose column of thirty grey corpses in mixed iron-red and hollow-green, walking in step. They share one slow cold light that shows between the ranks.

name: Scar Drake
lore: It hatched out of the plain itself and it has never eaten anything that was alive when it found it. A scar drake circles a burial detail for hours, low and patient, and comes down when the last shovel goes into the cart. It has learned the sound of the last shovel.
visualBrief: A lean winged drake the size of a horse, hide grey as turned earth, ribs showing through. The wings are patched with grave cloth grown into the membrane.

name: Ash-Sermon Speaker
lore: The Ash Prophet cannot be in six places, so he trains speakers and sends them out with the raids. A speaker preaches while the Column burns, and the preaching is the point; the burning is only the illustration. They are High-Tier, all of them, and they open warded gates for a living.
visualBrief: A soot-wrapped figure standing upright and still while everything around burns, arms spread, magic stones burning out in both fists. Relic-violet thread runs the length of the sleeves.

name: Crownfall Automaton
lore: It stood in the hall when the relic went off and it did not stop working. Whatever the relic did to the stone, it did to this as well; the brass runs cold and the magic stones in it have not needed changing in a generation. The Builder School would like it back. Nobody has offered to go and get it.
visualBrief: A tall ceremonial automaton in blackened plating, joints bleeding a thin violet light instead of lamp-glow. The crown device on its shield has been struck through.

name: Cinderfall Giant
lore: The Cindered say it was a man on the last day and they say it without arguing about which man. It walks the outer districts where the fires still find fuel and it will not enter the streets nearest the hall. Whatever it remembers, it remembers that much.
visualBrief: A giant of packed cinder and bone three men high, cracked open along the chest where a furnace glow shows. It leaves a trail of burning ash behind each step.

name: Afterglow Shade
lore: The violet light over the fallen city is not only light. Where it pools deep enough, it takes the shape of whoever last stood in that spot and keeps standing there. It is not the person and it never was. It knows their name and it will use it.
visualBrief: A person-shaped column of violet light with no features, only a suggestion of posture. It casts no shadow and makes no sound when it moves.

name: Icefloe Wyrm
lore: It swims under the shelf and comes up through it where the ice is thin. The expedition sounds the ice ahead of every sled for exactly this reason. A wyrm has taken a full sled team and the sounding pole they were using to check for it.
visualBrief: A wingless wyrm the length of four carts, scaled in overlapping pale plates like packed floe ice. The mouth opens in three parts and lines up with the crack it comes through.

name: Oathgate Sentinel
lore: The largest of the Stoneguard's carried pieces, and the one they set at the head of the ice camp. It holds a gate frame with no gate and no wall on either side. The Stoneguard stand their watch beside it and consider the arrangement correct.
visualBrief: A gate-wide iron figure with a shield in each hand and a stone lintel strapped across the shoulders. Frost fills every oath-letter cut into the armor.

name: Thorncrown Drake
lore: The old one the bramble drakes get out of the way for. It has lived in the deep veil long enough that the canes grow through its back plates and it carries a hedge on its spine. The bramble-kin route their lanes around it and have done for two generations.
visualBrief: A heavy four-legged drake the size of a barn, bark-brown plates with living black cane rooted along the spine. The head is crowned in thorn growth and old scarring.

name: Deepwater Hauler
lore: Gildmark harnessed them to warp hulls into the deepwater berth, back when the harbor was smaller and the ledger was thinner. Three broke their harness in one gale and never left the bay. The Harbor Council still lists them as assets in service.
visualBrief: A great grey sea beast the length of a ship's boat, harbor-fog hide scarred by tow rope. A rotted brass harness is grown into the flesh across the back.

name: Hollow-Bell Wight
lore: Norhollow's emblem is a hollow bell over crossed stakes, and the town has never explained the hollow bell to outsiders. This walks the moor above the palisade and makes a sound like one. Every guard on the line knows what the sound means. None of them will say it to a stranger.
visualBrief: A tall figure in frost-white palisade leathers with a rusted bell frame worn over the head, empty where the clapper should hang. Wind pours through the frame and does not stop.

name: Scarfield Sovereign
lore: The plain has been fed for four seasons and this is what four seasons buys. It holds the middle of the Ashvale Front and neither banner has crossed there since it stood up. The war has quietly moved to the flanks, and neither town has admitted why.
visualBrief: A towering shape of packed grave earth and layered mail three men high, a crown of broken banner poles fused into the shoulders. Cold black light burns in the chest cavity.

name: Boneorchard Warden
lore: Where the burial rows run deepest, the ground grew something that keeps them. It does not leave its rows and it does not let anything be taken out of them. Burial parties working that quarter dig new rows a mile away and do not argue about the extra mile.
visualBrief: A rooted mass of grey bone and grave timber the size of a house, spread wide rather than tall, with long reaching limbs. The rows around it are marked by upright shields sunk in the dirt.

name: Hallowed Toll-Warden
lore: The Bell School had one built to carry a tower bell onto the plain and ring the front clean without losing another warden company. It works. It has been out there for two seasons, ringing on the hour, and it will not answer a recall. The Bellfaith counts it a success and does not go near it.
visualBrief: A tall bronze-plated automaton carrying a full tower bell in a shoulder frame, striking arm raised. A steady pale light shows through the bell's mouth.

name: Relicdrawn Siege Hulk
lore: The ruler's own engines were in the yard when he used the relic, and the relic did not care whose they were. This is three of them run together and still trying to fire. The Column has tried to drive it out of the yard and toward the war towns twice. Both attempts are why there are fewer Column raiders this year.
visualBrief: A fused wreck of siege frames and iron the width of a street, walking on melted wheel stubs. White heat shows in the barrel throats; the outer shell is cinder-black.

name: Ashcrown Drake
lore: It roosts on the broken hall and it has fed on the afterglow since before anyone alive was born. The Ash Prophet preaches that it is the city's honest face. He has never once preached under it.
visualBrief: A great winged drake with cinder-black scale and a violet glow deep under the plates, roosting with the wings folded like a mantle. A ring of bare horn crowns the skull.

name: Whitewaste Colossus
lore: The far shelf holds one and the expedition's maps end where it walks. It has never come south and it has never let a survey team come north. There is a line on the master chart with no note beside it. Everyone at the camp knows what the line means.
visualBrief: A glacier-blue giant four men high, ice fused into slabs across the shoulders and back, moving with a slow grinding gait. The face is a smooth featureless plane of ice.

name: Heartwood Tyrant
lore: At the center of the veil is a tree the bramble runs out from, and the Bramble Mothers answer to it the way a wall answers to a foundation. The skirmishers do not have a name for it that they will give an outsider. They will only say the veil was here first and intends to stay.
visualBrief: A vast black-barked trunk with a mouth-shaped split at the base and root limbs that lift and set down like legs. Bramble grows outward from it in every direction for a hundred paces.

name: Harbor War-Beast
lore: The top of the Harbor Council's arms list, sold by the pair and shipped in a reinforced crate. One pair never made the manifest and never made the hold either. They have been in the coast hills above Gildmark since, and the Council has priced the loss and moved on.
visualBrief: A long-limbed running beast taller than a horse at the shoulder, tarnished gold barding riveted to the hide. Ward runes on the plates are worn smooth from use.

name: Gravefield Maw
lore: The whole low ground of the Ashvale Front, standing up at once. It does not walk so much as the field walks with it. Both towns have watched it from their own side of the plain and neither has sent anyone out to it, and neither has said so to the other.
visualBrief: An immense open mouth set in a rolling hill of grave earth, mail, and shattered timber, wider than a village square. Cold black light pours out of it and lies over the ground like fog.

name: Warscar Titan
lore: Four seasons of unburied dead, wearing four seasons of abandoned armor, standing at the head of the plain. It has never taken a step toward either town. It stands where the burying stopped and it does not permit the burying to start again.
visualBrief: A void-black figure five men high, armored in a shell of fused shields and breastplates from both banners. Where a face would be there is a hollow the size of a doorway.

name: Relicshell Colossus
lore: The relic was set off inside a building, and this is the building. Every stone of the hall took the blast and none of it fell. The Cindered will not look at it directly, and the ones who grew up elsewhere do not understand why until they see it once.
visualBrief: A walking hall of bone-white stone five men high, doorways and window slots still visible across the body. Every opening glows white from inside.

name: Crownash Wyrm
lore: It came out of the deepest ruin district a generation after the fall, already this size. It circles the fallen city and it has never once crossed the line where the afterglow ends. Whatever holds it there is the only reason the war towns still exist to argue with each other.
visualBrief: An immense wingless wyrm coiled through the broken streets, scales cinder-black shot through with violet. The head is crowned in a ring of bone spurs and trails ash from the jaws.

name: Lastbell Choir
lore: Every warden the Ashvale Front has taken, ringing together in one place. It moves across the plain in a slow line and it burns the void out of everything it passes, including the ground and including anyone standing on it. The Bellfaith does not claim it. The Bellfaith also does not deny that it is theirs.
visualBrief: A wide line of pale robed figures made of light, walking abreast, none of them fully solid. A single unbroken tolling sound moves with them.

name: Deepfrost Wyrm
lore: Under the far shelf there is water, and under the water there is this. It has surfaced twice in living memory and both times the ice road had to be surveyed again from the start. The expedition marks its two surfacing points on every chart and marks nothing else out that far.
visualBrief: A wyrm long enough to bridge a bay, plated in clear blue-white ice scale with a dark shape visible beneath. The jaws open in four parts and steam heavily in the cold.
